2610.10311.title: Fault-tolerant foundation models
2610.10311.paper_summary: Emerging computer hardware often trades reliability for energy efficiency; here we show that large-language models (LLMs) can be trained to tolerate this unreliability, and that rather than degrading, their error resilience actually increases as they grow. Modified neural scaling laws inferred from 40,000 GPU-hours of training runs on simulated faulty digital hardware quantify this trend and suggest that models learn to compute within "good" error-correcting codes, whose relative overhead remains finite no matter how large the model gets. This finding leads us to conjecture that appropriately trained LLMs may be formally fault-tolerant; if true, running AI inference on low energy, faulty hardware may be a path to substantial energy savings over the status quo.
2610.10311.paper_summary_zh: 新興的計算機硬體往往以可靠性換取能效；在這裡我們展示大型語言模型（LLMs）可以被訓練以容忍這種不可靠性，並且隨著它們的增長，其錯誤韌性實際上會增加，而不是下降。從 40,000 GPU 小時的模擬故障數位硬體訓練運行中推斷的修正神經擴展法則量化了這一趨勢，並表明模型學會在「良好」的錯誤更正碼內進行計算，無論模型多大，其相對開銷始終保持有限。這一發現使我們推測，適當訓練的 LLM 可能在形式上是容錯的；如果這是真的，在低能耗、故障硬體上運行 AI 推理可能是相較於現狀實現顯著節能的一條途徑。
